channel.description: An economy daily: central banks, growth and the companies that book the profit.

item.title: Economic Daily · November 13, 2026
item.description: Two hands reached in opposite directions today. At the Shanghai Stock Exchange's international investors conference the CSRC put three auditable numbers on the table: Rmb100bn of the third swap-facility tranche already deployed, more than Rmb600bn of A-shares bought by long-term money this year, and dividends plus buybacks now larger than IPO and refinancing proceeds. Hours later the NDRC cut petrol and diesel by Rmb645 and Rmb625 a tonne, while Brent rose 3.3% to US$95.82. One hand holds up the price of assets with rules; the other presses down the cost of energy. Both bills land on household balance sheets. CSRC: Rmb100bn of the third swap facility is deployed as long-term money buys over Rmb600bn of A-shares

item.title: Economic Daily · November 12, 2026
item.description: Today the price of money is being re-anchored. The PBOC's quarterly report wants loan pricing to move past a single LPR reference, with DR001 averaging 1.34% in the first nine months and new corporate loans just under 3.0%; the same session, a 63-day T-bill cleared at 1.05%, 20bp under the 1.25% overnight repo rate. Assets split behind it: ChiNext added 3.11%, the Hang Seng lost 0.98%. When the front end is pinned, whoever holds the duration pays for the price. PBOC Q3 report: loan pricing to move beyond a single LPR reference as DR001 averages 1.34%

item.title: Economic Daily · November 11, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is that the price of money moved first and assets re-sorted behind it. US October CPI came in above forecasts, markets priced a December hike at 100%, and the dollar and short-dated Treasuries rose together. The same evening, Alibaba put T-Head on a path to a Hong Kong listing, TSMC approved a $40.9bn capital budget, and the CIIE closed with $85.45bn of intended deals. The funding window is narrowing; only assets that can fund themselves get to negotiate. US October CPI rises 0.4% m/m, above forecasts: markets price a December hike at 100%

item.title: Economic Daily · November 10, 2026
item.description: Short money is being drained while long money comes due. The People's Bank of China lent only RMB 190bn overnight on November 10, after a RMB 44bn net drain the previous day, and November brings RMB 1.8tn of maturing MLF and outright reverse repos plus more than RMB 1.5tn of net government bond financing. On the same day, savings bonds opened at 1.63% and 1.7%, oil fell as much as 5.6%, October passenger car retail was down 27.1%, and one Nasdaq-100 ETF traded 21% above its net asset value. The price of money has not moved; the tenor at which you can get it has. Overnight reverse repos keep draining: RMB 190bn lent on November 10, with RMB 1.8tn of MLF and outright repos maturing in November

item.title: Economic Daily · November 9, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is upstream heat, downstream cold, and money looking for an exit in between. October CPI rose 0.7% year on year and PPI 5.7%, a five-point scissors gap: fresh vegetables at -16.9% and pork at -8.6% held consumer prices down, while coal at +36.6% and oil and gas at +35.0% pushed producer prices up. The same day, central SOEs signed more than $100bn at the import expo, and Japan's finance ministry disclosed ¥15.4tn of intervention in three days. The price split will end up as a redistribution on income statements. China's October CPI rises 0.7% y/y and PPI 5.7%, a five-point scissors gap

item.title: Economy Daily · November 8, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is that the story is running ahead of the ledger. Economic Daily took aim at solid-state battery marketing: Ouyang Minggao says everything claimed as industrialised is still a hybrid, the fastest sulphide route sits at TRL5, and the target for all-solid-state scale is 2030. Meanwhile Berkshire piled cash up to $377.4bn and bought back $9.6bn of stock, the Africa-China trade forum signed RMB 40.96bn of projects, and Shanghai's state-owned buyers placed $2.862bn of import-expo orders. Technology runs on TRL time; capital runs on quarterly time. Two regulators target online financial black markets, naming debt-avoidance, insurance-refund and credit-repair accounts

item.title: Economic Daily · November 7, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is who pays for a higher rate. US payrolls added 165,000 jobs in October and unemployment fell to 4.1%, with upward revisions of 84,000 and December hike odds at 76.8%. Beijing answered with cash flow: the State Council told ministries to get policy funds to grassroots and firms on time and to formalise the market-stabilisation mechanism, while October reserves rose $4.9 billion to $3.4052 trillion. Hong Kong fell 1.27%, excavator sales growth slowed to 11.8%, and CNOOC signed $13.6 billion of CIIE purchase deals. Data sets the rate; balance sheets absorb the bill. US payrolls add 165,000 in October, unemployment falls to 4.1% and December hike odds reach 76.8%

item.title: Economic Daily · November 6, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is the discount rate. US stocks crashed on November 5: the Nasdaq fell 5.52%, the Dow lost 1,833 points and tech dropped 7.30%. The Bank of England raised Bank Rate 25bp to 4% on an 8-1 vote, with energy doing the pushing. A-shares followed on November 6, ChiNext down 3.96% on shrinking turnover, while the PBOC fully satisfied 226 billion yuan of overnight reverse repos. Politics changed the discount rate, not this quarter's earnings. US stocks crash on November 5: Nasdaq down 5.52%, Dow down 1,833 points

item.title: Economic Daily · November 5, 2026
item.description: Regime change, a war premium unwinding and a liquidity drain arrived on the same day. Democrats won both chambers of Congress; oil gave back its war premium, with Brent settling 8.67% lower at $94.62. In China, the PBOC’s 30 billion yuan three-month outright reverse repo runs against 50 billion yuan maturing — a net withdrawal of 20 billion, even as DR001 fell to 1.2591%. Politics flipped, risk premium loosened, liquidity tightened. Democrats win both chambers of Congress: 258 House seats projected, at least seven Senate seats flipped

item.title: Economic Daily · November 4, 2026
item.description: The last mile of inflation is the story. Australia’s central bank lifted its cash rate for the fifth time this year, to 4.85%, on a 6-3 vote and marked its inflation peak up to 4.5% — the cost of money stays higher for longer. Beijing’s ledger reads differently: the State Council’s financial work report showed 33 trillion yuan of new social financing over twelve months, while the PBOC ran a 100 billion yuan swap facility for non-banks at a 10bp fee. After the US close, AMD guided fourth-quarter revenue to $17 billion and Aramco’s cash flow improved on refining spreads. Price and duration, repriced on the same day. RBA raises the cash rate to 4.85% on a 6-3 vote and lifts its inflation peak to 4.5%

item.title: Economic Daily · November 3, 2026
item.description: Two directions in the same session: the PBOC drained foreign-currency liquidity by lifting the FX deposit reserve ratio from 4% to 6%, then cut the rate on buyback relending to 1% and made the facility permanent. Abroad the script runs the other way — the Fed held rates on a 10-2 vote while markets still price an 85% chance of a December hike, oil fell 7.36% in a night, and Apple guided gross margin down to 45–46%. Both sides are repricing money. The PBOC lifts the FX deposit reserve ratio to 6% from 4%, effective November 15

item.title: Economic Daily · November 2, 2026
item.description: Today’s thread is about moving the clock forward: the Finance Ministry brings part of the 2027 local-bond quota into January, and ¥5.1 trillion of nine-month profit includes a 281% jump in AI earnings. The car market is splitting the other way — Leapmotor and Xpeng set records while Nio and Li Auto fell on both counts. Policy moves early; companies diverge. Beijing brings the 2027 local-bond quota forward: 60% cap, issuance from January

item.title: Economic Daily · November 1, 2026
item.description: China’s October manufacturing PMI slipped to 49.3, with output and new orders both contracting and high-tech manufacturing the lone bright spot at 51.3. The same day, 42 listed banks reported 7.79% revenue growth and 3.78% profit growth at a 1.55% net interest margin. The cycle is cooling; the accounting is being rewritten. October PMI at 49.3: output and orders both fall, while prices stay in expansion

item.title: Economic Daily · October 31, 2026
item.description: The central bank moved its policy anchor from seven days to overnight: from November 2 it will tender 1.25% overnight reverse repos every working day. The same session, 30-year T-bond futures fell 0.94% while the Nasdaq dropped 2.86% and Intel 28.58%. New trust rules shut the door on guarantees and pooled funds, while the exchange approved RMB 36.6 billion of project bonds for two developers. The price of money is being re-anchored; the channels are being switched. The PBoC re-anchors policy at overnight: 1.25% reverse repos, every working day from November 2

item.title: Economic Daily · October 30, 2026
item.description: No single headline today, just three sets of books: the central bank plugged the month-end funding gap with RMB 1 trillion of overnight money; Shanghai's financing mix moved another 10 points toward bonds and equity; and of 2,862 Shenzhen earnings reports, fewer than half showed growth — optical modules up 200%, chipmaking equipment up 5.10%. Money is still moving, but it is moving through fewer channels. RMB 1 trillion overnight: the PBoC bridges month-end without cutting rates
